rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Inter‑subject variability in autonomic reactivity causes the nonconformity scores to be systematically miscalibrated for high‑reactivity individuals.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: High‑reactivity subjects will show systematically higher nonconformity scores and smaller prediction sets than low‑reactivity subjects, even after controlling for baseline HRV and medication.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: High‑reactivity subjects have noisier physiological signals, which inflates the variance of nonconformity scores without a systematic calibration bias.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: The distribution of nonconformity scores for high‑reactivity subjects will be wider but centered similarly to low‑reactivity subjects; prediction set sizes will not differ after adjusting for signal‑to‑noise ratio.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Compare nonconformity score means and variances across reactivity quantiles before and after normalizing each subject's scores by their within‑subject signal‑to‑noise ratio.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Mean nonconformity scores remain significantly higher for high‑reactivity subjects after SNR normalization.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Mean scores become indistinguishable across reactivity groups after SNR normalization, while variances converge.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Sensor‑specific drift in the wrist‑worn EDA channel during prolonged recordings leads to biased nonconformity estimates for later trials.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Nonconformity scores will increase monotonically with trial index, and coverage will drop for later trials even when controlling for habituation.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Late‑session undercoverage is driven by participant habituation to the stressor, not by sensor drift.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: Nonconformity scores will correlate with trial index only when habituation markers (e.g., reduced EDA peak amplitude) are present; controlling for habituation removes the trial‑order effect.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Fit a mixed‑effects model with trial index and habituation metric (EDA peak amplitude) as predictors of nonconformity score; compare model fit with and without a sensor‑drift proxy (impedance or SNR).
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Trial index remains a significant predictor after accounting for habituation, and impedance/SNR adds explanatory power.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Habituation metric fully mediates the trial‑index effect; impedance/SNR does not improve model fit.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Non‑stationary heart‑rate variability (HRV) dynamics across the stress‑recovery cycle violate the exchangeability assumption within Mondrian strata.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Autocorrelation of nonconformity residuals will be significant within transitional windows, and coverage will be lowest for those windows.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Transitional periods simply have fewer calibration samples, causing a small‑stratum effect rather than a violation of exchangeability.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: Coverage deficits will disappear when stratum‑specific calibration sample size is matched across transitional and stable periods.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Create balanced calibration subsets by down‑sampling stable periods to match transitional sample counts; recompute coverage for each period type.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Coverage remains lower for transitional periods even with equal calibration sample sizes.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Coverage equalizes across period types after sample‑size matching.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Mislabeling of self‑reported stress levels for a subset of participants introduces systematic label noise into the Mondrian categories.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Subjects with low self‑report consistency will show systematically narrower nonconformity distributions in the low‑stress stratum, leading to undercoverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Physiological signals are genuinely ambiguous for some subjects, causing overlapping feature distributions that the taxonomy cannot separate.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: Nonconformity distributions for inconsistent reporters will overlap with both stress strata, but the degree of overlap will not correlate with self‑report consistency metrics.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Compute stratum‑wise nonconformity overlap (e.g., Bhattacharyya coefficient) and correlate with per‑subject self‑report reliability scores.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Higher overlap strongly correlates with lower self‑report reliability.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Overlap is high for certain subjects regardless of reliability scores, and reliability does not predict overlap.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Insufficient representation of certain demographic sub‑groups (e.g., age > 50) in the calibration set leads to stratum‑specific undercoverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Coverage will be significantly lower for older age deciles, and adding age as a stratification variable will restore nominal coverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: The apparent age effect is mediated by fitness level; older participants tend to be less fit, and fitness—not age—drives the coverage gap.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: When fitness (e.g., VO2 max or activity level) is included as a covariate, the age‑coverage relationship disappears.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Fit a logistic regression predicting per‑subject coverage with age, fitness, and their interaction; compare models with and without fitness.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Age remains a significant predictor after adjusting for fitness.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Fitness fully accounts for the coverage difference; age effect becomes non‑significant.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: The choice of nonconformity score (e.g., softmax margin) is poorly aligned with the multimodal feature geometry for stress classification.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Alternative nonconformity scores that respect feature correlations (e.g., Mahalanobis distance) will yield higher coverage without increasing prediction set size excessively.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Undercoverage stems from distribution shift between calibration and test sets, not from the nonconformity score itself.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: All nonconformity scores will show similar coverage deficits when evaluated on shifted test data; improvements only appear after correcting the shift.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Evaluate multiple nonconformity scores on both original and covariate‑shift‑corrected test sets (e.g., using importance weighting).
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Mahalanobis‑based score improves coverage on the original test set, while margin‑based score does not.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: All scores improve equally after shift correction, and none improves on the uncorrected set.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Batch effects from different recording days cause distribution shift that is not captured by the Mondrian condition labels.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Nonconformity scores will differ systematically across recording days, and day‑aware stratification will restore coverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Day‑level differences are actually due to habituation across days (participants become less reactive), not ambient batch effects.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: Including trial‑order‑within‑day as a covariate eliminates day effects; day‑specific strata add no further benefit.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage of three models: (1) condition‑only strata, (2) condition+day strata, (3) condition+day+trial‑order strata.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Model (2) significantly improves coverage over (1), and (3) does not improve further.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Model (3) improves coverage over (2), indicating trial‑order (habituation) explains the day effect.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Physiological habituation across repeated stress trials reduces signal discriminability, but the Mondrian taxonomy treats each trial as identically distributed.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Nonconformity scores will decrease (indicating higher confidence) across trial order while coverage drops, and trial‑aware strata will recover coverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Apparent habituation is confounded by sensor drift that worsens over the session, not by true physiological adaptation.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: Signal quality metrics (e.g., EDA SNR) will degrade with trial order; controlling for SNR removes the trial‑order effect on nonconformity scores.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Regress nonconformity score on trial index and SNR; test whether trial index remains significant after SNR inclusion.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Trial index stays significant after controlling for SNR.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Trial index becomes non‑significant once SNR is in the model.

rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_hypothesis: Correlated missingness in the respiration belt (e.g., motion artifacts) creates informative missingness that the conformal predictor ignores.
rival_prediction_matrix.meno_j_prediction: Windows with missing respiration data during high‑movement stress will have higher nonconformity scores and lower coverage than complete‑case windows.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_explanation: Missingness is random with respect to stress level; coverage loss is simply due to reduced feature dimensionality, not informative missingness.
rival_prediction_matrix.rival_prediction: Coverage will be equally reduced for any randomly removed modality, and missingness indicators will not predict nonconformity scores beyond the loss of features.
rival_prediction_matrix.distinguishing_test: Simulate random missingness of respiration in low‑movement windows and compare coverage to actual high‑movement missingness; also test a missingness‑aware nonconformity score.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_meno_j: Actual high‑movement missingness yields lower coverage than simulated random missingness, and missingness‑aware score restores coverage.
rival_prediction_matrix.what_result_supports_rival: Coverage loss matches random missingness simulation, and missingness indicator adds no predictive value.
